sections.label: Workplace Fairness Bill protections
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness Bill is designed to improve protections against workplace discrimination while preserving fair and harmonious workplace norms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Instead, we should take proactive steps to ensure that employees and jobseekers in Singapore continue to be assured of fair treatment in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This Workplace Fairness Bill has therefore been designed to improve protections against workplace discrimination, while preserving our fair and harmonious workplace norms.

sections.label: Tripartite Committee consultations
sections.summary: The Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness held more than 70 in-person engagements with over 2,000 individuals from various groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness also consulted widely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have held more than 70 in-person engagements, with more than 2,000 individuals from all walks of life – including unions, workers, employers, human resources (HR) and legal professionals, and civil society and community organisations.

sections.label: Five protected characteristics chosen
sections.summary: After extensive consultations, five categories of protected characteristics under clause 8 were chosen, covering over 95% of discrimination complaints.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: After extensive consultations, we have decided on a more nuanced and calibrated approach by first starting with five categories of protected characteristics under clause 8.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Together, they account for more than 95% of discrimination complaints received by TAFEP and the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

sections.label: Fair Consideration Framework codified
sections.summary: Clause 26 codifies existing Fair Consideration Framework job advertisement requirements and the duty to fairly consider candidates into law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Separately, clause 26 codifies into law the existing Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) job advertisement requirements and the duty to fairly consider candidates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: By doing so, we will have a greater range of enforcement levers calibrated to the severity of the breaches and further deter discriminatory employers.

sections.label: Women in STEM jobs
sections.summary: Women in STEM jobs rose from 29% in 2013 to 34% in 2023 over a 10-year horizon.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Women in STEM jobs were 29% in 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: However, this improved to 34% in 2023 over a 10-year horizon.

sections.label: Disability discrimination and hiring exception
sections.summary: The Bill prohibits discrimination against disabilities and clause 24 allows employers to favour persons with disabilities in hiring.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Bill complements the Government's Enabling Masterplan 2030 by prohibiting discrimination against disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Clause 24 also provides an exception to facilitate greater employment opportunities for this group by allowing employers to favour persons with disabilities in their hiring decisions.

sections.label: Bill complements TGFEP
sections.summary: The Bill complements TGFEP, enabling TAFEP to tackle workplace discrimination based on all other characteristics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Bill complements TGFEP, which will enable TAFEP to tackle workplace discrimination based on all other characteristics.

sections.label: Firms with discrimination procedures
sections.summary: Six in 10 firms already have formal procedures to manage workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Today, six in 10 firms already have formal procedures to manage workplace discrimination.

sections.label: Clause 27 grievance inquiry
sections.summary: Clause 27 requires firms to inquire into grievances received, review them and inform the employee of the result.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Clause 27 of the Bill requires firms to inquire into the grievance they have received, review it and inform the employee of the result.

sections.label: Clause 28 anti-retaliation protection
sections.summary: Clause 28 prohibits employers from retaliating against those who file complaints and claims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Clause 28 of the Bill provides better assurance by prohibiting employers from retaliating against those that file complaints and claims.

sections.label: WFL implementation and mediation
sections.summary: If both Bills pass, WFL is intended for 2026 or 2027, with mediation before unresolved cases proceed to claims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: If both Bills are passed, we intend to implement the WFL sometime in 2026 or 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For cases that cannot be resolved through the firms' grievance handling process, we intend for the parties to go through mediation before a workplace discrimination claim proceeds.

sections.label: Clause 4 small firm exemption
sections.summary: Clause 4 exempts firms with fewer than 25 employees, giving them more time to build capabilities before WFL applies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill exempts firms with fewer than 25 employees, who will be given more time to build up their capabilities before the WFL requirements apply to them.

sections.label: Enforcement against errant employers
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Government to take enforcement action against errant employers based on the severity of the breach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For the small number of errant employers that blatantly flout the rules, the Bill empowers the Government to take enforcement action based on the severity of the breach.

sections.label: Strengthening workplace protections
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens existing workplace protections against discrimination for employees and job seekers on listed grounds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Bill will strengthen existing workplace protections, ensuring employees and job seekers are not discriminated due to age, nationality, sex, marital or pregnancy status, caregiving responsibilities, race, religion, language, disability or mental health conditions.

sections.label: Small business temporary exemption
sections.summary: Small businesses with fewer than 25 employees will be temporarily exempted from the Bill for the first five years after implementation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Small businesses with fewer than 25 employees will be temporarily exempted from the Bill for the first five years after implementation, giving them more time to adapt to the new regulations.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness legislation norms
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness legislation will help preserve and enhance fair and harmonious norms that have worked well thus far.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To my Malay speaking colleagues and friends, please pardon my errors in delivery and pronunciation. :   The Workplace Fairness legislation will help preserve and enhance the fair and harmonious norms that have worked well thus far.

sections.label: Additional layer of protection
sections.summary: The Bill is an additional layer of protection ensuring workers are evaluated and hired on abilities, with recourse available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Instead, it is an additional layer of measured protection that helps to ensure workers are evaluated and hired based on their abilities and not discriminatory biases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For employees and jobseekers, this Bill sends a strong message – everyone has an opportunity to fulfil their potential at work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It will ensure that there is recourse available and no worker should have to suffer in silence – such as in cases where they face racial or religious discrimination at work.

sections.label: Education-first approach to enforcement
sections.summary: An education-first approach will be taken, with action only against employers that blatantly flout the rules.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this new legislation, we will take an education-first approach.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will only take action against employers that blatantly flout the rules. : To conclude, while this Bill is not a silver bullet for upholding workplace fairness, it will enhance our current model of promoting fair and harmonious workplaces in a way that is tailored to our local context.

sections.label: Protection from employment discrimination
sections.summary: The Bill protects individuals from employer discrimination based on listed protected characteristics and ensures Singaporeans and PRs are fairly considered for employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, to protect individuals from discrimination by employers on the grounds of the protected characteristics listed in clause 8, covering age, nationality, sex, marital status, pregnancy, caregiving responsibilities, race, religion, language, ability, disability and mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, and very significantly, in my view, it ensures that Singaporeans and Permanent Residents (PRs) are fairly considered for employment opportunities and continue to form the core of the workforce in Singapore, with foreigners as a complement.

sections.label: Clause 22 Singaporean PR preference
sections.summary: Clause 22 states it is not discrimination to reserve an employment opportunity for a Singaporean or PR over a foreigner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 22 reads that it is not discrimination to say that an employment opportunity is for a Singaporean or PR at the expense of someone who is a foreigner.

sections.label: Associated discrimination clause explained
sections.summary: The clause states an employment decision made only on a protected characteristic of a relative or associate is not discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This clause deals with what is commonly referred to as "associated discrimination" and it reads, "an employment decision made only on the ground of a protected characteristic of a relative or an associate of the individual is not discrimination".

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This reads rather innocently until one peruses the explanatory statement to the clause at the end of the Bill, which reads, I quote, "An employer does not discriminate against A if the employer dismisses A on the ground of the race of A's husband." Prima facie and without more, this explanation makes it clear to me, at least, that A's employer is a racist.

sections.label: Workplace coverage timeline
sections.summary: If the Bill comes into force in 2026, all workplaces would only be covered in 2031 at the earliest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If this Bill comes into force in 2026, for example, it follows that all our workplaces will only be covered in 2031 at the earliest.

sections.label: Small firm threshold and coverage
sections.summary: Workers in companies with fewer than 25 individuals will not be covered by clause 28 for at least five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the intent of MOM is that firms with less than 25 workers will continue to be covered by the guidelines, the Minister confirmed that between 2018 and 2022, 35% of workplace discrimination complaints were received from workers working in firms with a headcount of less than 25.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For clarity, can the Minister confirm if the threshold number of 25 is to be understood on a group basis for companies that have a holding company and multiple corporate entities for corporate planning and risk management purposes, but effectively operate as one entity or for an individual corporate entity, such as a company?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And in addition to this, are the Civil Service and public service officers, including uniformed services and Statutory Boards, also covered by this Bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As it stands, workers who are employed by companies with less than 25 individuals will not be covered by clause 28, at least for the next five years.

sections.label: Penalties for civil contraventions
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Bill sets specific penalties for civil contraventions or an open-ended range.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify if the Bill contemplates a specific penalty amount for each of the civil contraventions listed in clause 31(1)(a) to (i), or is there an open-ended range of penalties, for example, up to $5,000 for any contravention?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, clause 34 of the Bill covers the specific penalty amount that will be imposed on an employer in the case of a serious civil contravention – $50,000 for a first order and $250,000 for subsequent cases.

sections.label: Litigation and TAFEP complaints
sections.summary: Litigation can be necessary in egregious cases, and from 2018 to 2022 nationality and age discrimination were the top TAFEP complaints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, litigation can be necessary when egregious cases present themselves and workers are on the receiving end of the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We know that between 2018 and 2022, the two protected characteristics that host the most number of complaints to TAFEP were discrimination by nationality and discrimination by age.

sections.label: Second workplace fairness Bill
sections.summary: The Government announced a second Bill on workplace fairness introducing procedural rights and processes for private claims under this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To conclude, Mr Speaker, the Government has announced that there will be a second Bill associated with workplace fairness, which will introduce the procedural rights and processes for individuals to make private claims under this Bill.

sections.label: WP support for the Bill
sections.summary: Some Singaporeans felt the shift took too long amid discontent over nationality and age, but WP will support this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For some Singaporeans, the signalling of this philosophical shift has taken too long, particularly when one recalls the deep discontent over the last decade or so of some Singaporeans over perceptions of being overlooked by some employers on the grounds of nationality, in particular, but also age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Late, though it is, the change is for the better and WP will support this Bill.

sections.label: PME Taskforce findings and recommendations
sections.summary: The Taskforce found age bias and insufficient levelling of the playing field, recommended dedicated legislation, and this Bill addresses workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Taskforce found that 67% of mature PMEs aged 40 and above cited age-related bias as a key challenge in job search; and those in the modern services sector, that is, infocomm technology, professional services and financial services, in particular, thought current policies were insufficient in creating a level playing field with foreign PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: One of the key recommendations of the PME Taskforce was the need for a dedicated piece of legislation to prevent discriminatory practices that might arise from cost-driven or biased decisions, such as favouring foreign workers who may accept lower wages or are of a certain national origin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Their sentiments correspond with the nationally published statistics that age and nationality discrimination were the top two complaints received by TAFEP and MOM from 2018 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This Bill is watershed and landmark as it is a new and dedicated piece of legislation to address workplace discrimination across several important protected characteristics whether pre-employment, during employment and post-employment, such as during terminations or retrenchments.

sections.label: Clause 4(1)(b) employer exclusions
sections.summary: Clause 4(1)(b) excludes prescribed employers, and the Minister was asked about plans and grounds for such exclusions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Clause 4(1)(b) states that the Act will not apply to "any prescribed employer or class of employers".

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Could the Minister clarify if there are any current plans to exclude any employer or class of employers; and on what grounds would such employers be excluded?

sections.label: Clause 12 infant age range
sections.summary: The passage asks what the age range for an "infant" is in clause 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In clause 12, what is the age range for an "infant"?

sections.label: Employer grievance process requirements
sections.summary: Clause 27 requires employers to develop written processes to inquire, review, inform, keep records of and maintain confidentiality of grievances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Clause 27 requires employers to develop processes in writing to inquire, review, inform, keep records of and maintain confidentiality of grievances.

sections.label: IHRP certification update on WFL
sections.summary: The speaker submits that IHRP certification should be updated after the Bill is passed to cover WFL, tripartism and industrial relations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It is essential for the HR fraternity to be familiar with tripartism, industrial relations as well as this new piece of workplace fairness legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It is therefore, submitted that the IHRP certification should also be updated after the Bill is passed to cover WFL across all certifiable levels, including as an additional module for HR professionals with an internationally recognised HR certification but who may have missed covering topics, such as the WFL, tripartism and industrial relations in Singapore.

sections.label: Decline in discrimination help-seeking
sections.summary: MOM's Fair Employment Practices report shows a decline from 2022 to 2023 in employees seeking help for workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: According to MOM's Fair Employment Practices report, from 2022 to 2023, there was a decline in employees seeking help when faced with discrimination at work.

sections.label: Union representation for PMEs
sections.summary: The speaker calls for the Industrial Relations Act to be amended so unions can provide limited representation for PMEs in disputes under this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This is why it is critical to ensure that our unions are able to represent our workers, especially PMEs when they face workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We therefore call for the Industrial Relations Act to be amended, so that unions can provide limited representation for PMEs regarding disputes under this Bill.

sections.label: Enhancing protection against workplace harassment
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to complement existing harassment laws with extra-legal levers such as research, education and awareness training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: While recognising that this Bill makes harassment a type of grievance and that some remedies are currently possible under the Protection from Harassment Act, I would call on the Government to complement existing harassment laws by enhancing extra-legal levers to strengthen protection against workplace harassment, such as more research, education and awareness training on this very important issue.

sections.label: Queries on Bill's scope exclusions
sections.summary: The speaker queries why the Government scoped the legislation to exclude discrimination outside the workplace, indirect discrimination, other protected characteristics and several worker categories.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: She further said that Singapore has better employment statistics for women and seniors than some other developed nations, and the threat of getting Work Pass privileges revoked was an extremely serious one.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, given the use of the term "fairness" in today's Bill, I am glad that the Government has come round to the view that signals and ethical stances are important in tackling discrimination in the workplace and above all, it is important to legislate to outlaw such practices as illegal.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In my speech today, I would like to make some queries to understand why the Government decided to scope the legislation to: one, exclude discrimination outside the workplace; two, exclude indirect discrimination; three, exclude several other protected characteristics that the public has called for protections on; and four, exclude several categories of workers.

sections.label: PES status and discrimination
sections.summary: A concern is raised that National Service PES status may be used to discriminate against male candidates with non-visible disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Another concern that has been raised is the use of National Service Physical Employment Standard (PES) status to potentially discriminate against male candidates with non-visible disabilities, such as intellectual disabilities or neurodivergent conditions.

sections.label: Disproportionate impact and employer onus
sections.summary: The principle is that an apparently neutral criterion with a disproportionately negative impact on a protected group puts the onus on the employer to show genuine necessity.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The principle is that if an apparently neutral criterion or practice has a disproportionately negative impact on a group defined by race, religion, gender or other protected traits, the onus should be on the employer to demonstrate a genuine necessity for that criterion.

sections.label: Excluded workers under section 4(3)
sections.summary: Under the proposed section 4(3), platform workers are explicitly excluded from discrimination protections, and foreign domestic workers also appear not covered.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under the proposed section 4(3), platform workers are explicitly excluded from the protections from discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Foreign domestic workers also appear to not be covered because domestic workers are not covered by the Employment Act.

sections.label: Timeline for reasonable accommodations
sections.summary: Given the Government's 40% employment target for PwDs by 2030, the question asks for a timeline to recognise denial of reasonable accommodations as prohibited discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given the Government's own target to increase the employment rate of PwDs to 40% by 2030, I believe that this is a key policy lever to ensure that PwDs have a fair chance in joining the workforce and thriving at work.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Will the Government commit to a timeline to recognising the denial of reasonable accommodations as a prohibited form of discrimination under the Workplace Fairness Act within the next five years?

sections.label: Exploring mandated reasonable accommodations
sections.summary: The question asks how the Government proposes to explore mandating reasonable accommodations, given it has resisted legislating them and advisory approaches can be ignored.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As the Government has resisted the call to legislate reasonable accommodations for now, how then does it propose to explore how reasonable accommodations can be mandated and not just through an advisory which can be ignored?

sections.label: Bill's gaps and tokenism risk
sections.summary: The Bill excludes non-workplace discrimination, uses a narrow definition, leaves some groups without clear protection, and risks being seen as tokenistic.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It demonstrates that we, as a society, are prepared to take a stronger stance against discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But the Bill excludes significant scenarios of non-workplace discrimination, offers narrow definition of discrimination that leave out indirect and associational forms and leaves entire groups, such as platform workers, migrant domestic workers and people with certain disabilities without clear legislative protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Crucially, we risk creating a law that the public might view as tokenistic rather than genuinely transformative.

sections.label: Strengthening laws against discrimination
sections.summary: The passage calls for robust laws addressing real-world discrimination and openness to future scope expansions and accommodations.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must ensure that the laws are truly robust, that they address real-world discrimination comprehensively and that the Government remains open to future expansions of its scope.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope that we will address these gaps to consider future amendments that might strengthen protection for the groups left out and to ensure that reasonable accommodation are not relegated to a footnote.

sections.label: Age discrimination top workplace complaint
sections.summary: TAFEP figures show age discrimination was the most cited workplace discrimination form in 2023, ahead of race and gender complaints.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In 2023, age discrimination was the most commonly cited form of workplace discrimination according to TAFEP figures and is placed ahead of complaints about race discrimination and gender discrimination.

sections.label: Older workers share of workforce
sections.summary: Workers aged 50 and above make up about 37% of Singapore's resident workforce, a substantial portion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In Singapore, workers aged 50 and above account for approximately 37% of our resident workforce and this is a substantial portion that cannot be overlooked.

sections.label: WFL age protections and exceptions
sections.summary: Under the WFL, age is protected, barring adverse decisions based solely on age, while allowing policies favouring older workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Under the WFL, age is recognised as a protected characteristic, meaning that employers cannot make adverse employment decisions based solely on a person's age.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The WFL not only prohibits discriminatory practices but it also allows for policies that favour older workers in certain contexts.

sections.label: Schemes for age-friendly workplaces
sections.summary: Government schemes and tripartite initiatives let employers and unions create age-friendly workplaces and competitive multi-generational workforces.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Through various Government schemes and tripartite initiatives, including the NTUC's Company Training Committee and various job redesign grants, employers can work together with their unions to create age-friendly workplaces and businesses can ensure that their multi-generational workforce remains competitive and well-equipped to meet the challenges of the future.

sections.label: Tackling age bias in hiring
sections.summary: The passage urges vigilance against algorithmic bias, training recruiters, avoiding ageist AI filters, and a multi-faceted approach to age discrimination.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And depending on the way in which their algorithms are determined, that can inadvertently also introduce bias into the process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is important that employers be vigilant about these potential downsides and take concrete action to make sure that their human recruiters are properly selected and trained and briefed and that their AI filters and hiring algorithms avoid ageist biases so that the companies can benefit from capable candidates, regardless of their age and give all candidates a fair shot at securing employment and that their organisation can bring on the best candidate to serve its purpose.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: As our workforce ages, it is critical that we address the barriers that prevent older workers from accessing good jobs that bar them from training opportunities and deprive them of fair career progression.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This requires a multi-faceted approach, combining strong legal protections, age-friendly workplace practices and ongoing efforts at the tripartite level and in each workplace to promote inclusivity and diversity in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Ultimately, fighting age discrimination is not only a legal matter nor is it just a moral imperative.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: It is also an economic necessity that will help sustain long-term prosperity for all.

sections.label: Associated discrimination and WFL penalty
sections.summary: The speaker says discrimination is not tolerated and TAFEP will take up associated discrimination cases, but the Bill's prescribed penalty does not cover them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I would just like to provide one point of clarification to the Leader of the Opposition's earlier point on associated discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I want to, first and foremost, reassure every Member in the House and every Singaporean that we do not tolerate any form of discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: By virtue of the way the Member has described it, Mr Speaker, Sir, from the Leader of the Opposition, in terms of the associated discrimination, by virtue of the fact that an employee is married to someone who is of a different race, let us say, for example, who feels that he is being discriminated against because he is dismissed, TAFEP will take it up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But for the purpose of the prescribed penalty in terms of the Bill, WFL, at this particular point in time, we have not crafted it such that it is covered.

sections.label: TAFEP basis for WFL Bill
sections.summary: TAFEP is the basis for the WFL and will keep assisting workers experiencing workplace discrimination beyond the Bill's scope, which is a first legislative step.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: TAFEP was the basis on which we built this WFL on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: It will continue to assist any worker who experiences workplace discrimination even if they fall outside or beyond the scope of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This Bill is, really, the first step in introducing legislation for our workplace fairness regime.

sections.label: Workers' Party relief on MOM decision
sections.summary: Workers' Party MPs and Singaporeans feel relieved that MOM finally made this decision, with protection covering recruitment, employment and dismissal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We, the Workers' Party MPs, along with Singaporeans, feel relieved that after waiting for so long, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has finally made this decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This protection covers all stages of employment, including recruitment, period of employment and dismissal.

sections.label: Muslim men rejected over Friday prayers
sections.summary: Two situations involve Muslim men rejected at interviews for Friday prayer requests and Muslim male employees refused longer Friday breaks by employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One situation involves Muslim men being rejected for employment during interviews because their request to perform Friday prayers is not granted by the company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second situation involves Muslim male employees whose request for a slightly longer break on Fridays to perform Friday prayers are refused by their employers.

sections.label: Muslim worker told to remove hijab
sections.summary: A 2020 incident involved a Muslim female worker at a well-known department store told to remove her hijab shortly after starting her first day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moving forward, a recent incident that received attention from many people, including Madam Halimah Yacob, who was the President at that time, was a case that occurred in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It involved a Muslim female worker at a well-known department store who was told to remove her hijab a few minutes after she had just started work on her first day.

sections.label: Five protected characteristics covered
sections.summary: After over three years of research, consultation and revision, the Bill addresses five protected characteristics covering 95% of workplace complaints received.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: After more than three years of research, public consultation and thoughtful revision, it addresses five protected characteristics: nationality, age, sex/marital status/pregnancy status/caregiving responsibilities, race/religion/language and disability/mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Together, these cover 95% of workplace complaints received.

sections.label: PwD employment rate 2023
sections.summary: As of 2023, the employment rate for working-age PwDs exceeded 32%, about 32.7%, with over 600 companies adopting inclusive hiring practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As of 2023, the employment rate for working-age PwDs exceeded 32%, it is about 32.7%, with over 600 companies adopting inclusive hiring practices.

sections.label: Bill's narrow disability definition
sections.summary: The Bill's current definition of disability is too narrow, covering only autism, intellectual disabilities, physical disabilities and sensory disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Bill’s current definition of disability is too narrow, covering only autism, intellectual disabilities, physical disabilities and sensory disabilities.

sections.label: Tripartite Advisory lacks enforceability
sections.summary: The current proposal for a Tripartite Advisory on reasonable accommodations is a good start, but it lacks enforceability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The current proposal for a Tripartite Advisory on reasonable accommodations is a good start, but it lacks enforceability.

sections.label: Roadmap for legislation by 2030
sections.summary: Successful policies like the Compulsory Education Act show phase-by-phase legislation following public education can drive change, leading to a proposal for a roadmap for legislation by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Successful policies in Singapore, like our Compulsory Education Act, have shown that phase-by-phase legislation following public education can indeed drive meaningful change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So that leads to my third proposal, which is developing a roadmap for legislation by 2030 in this space.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Masterplan for PwDs
sections.summary: Fourth, to develop a SkillsFuture Masterplan for PwDs for them to upskill and remain competitive and not be left behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Fourth, to develop a SkillsFuture Masterplan for PwDs for them to upskill and remain competitive and not be left behind.

sections.label: Roadmap mandating accommodations by 2030
sections.summary: Readiness concerns are valid but must not delay progress indefinitely, so the House is urged to support a clear roadmap mandating reasonable accommodations by 2030, aligned with the expiration of the current Enabling Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: While readiness concerns are valid, they must not delay progress indefinitely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, I urge the House to support a clear roadmap that mandates reasonable accommodations by 2030, aligned with the expiration of the current Enabling Masterplan for the disabled.

sections.label: Protected characteristics and 5% gap
sections.summary: Clause 8 prohibits discrimination based on 11 protected characteristics covering 95% of MOM and TAFEP complaints, leaving 5% without legal protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on clause 8 of the Bill, employers are prohibited from discrimination on the basis of 11 protected characteristics, which form 95% of the workplace discrimination complaints received by MOM and TAFEP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Are we not then discriminating against this 5% in not according them adequate legal protection?

sections.label: Data use and medical discrimination
sections.summary: The Bill would disallow data use to assess employment suitability, raising whether it prohibits unjustified discrimination based on medical condition or history.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It would also explicitly disallow data to be used to assess one's suitability for employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, would this Bill also prohibit employers from discrimination based on one's medical condition or medical history if unjustified?

sections.label: Criminal record discrimination consideration
sections.summary: Over 20 years after the Yellow Ribbon project launched in June 2004, the question asks if Government would consider prohibiting discrimination based on criminal record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that it has been more than 20 years since the Yellow Ribbon project was launched in June 2004, would the Government also consider prohibiting discrimination on the basis of one's criminal record?

sections.label: No protection against indirect discrimination
sections.summary: The Bill does not protect workers against indirect discrimination, meaning neutral policies that disadvantage certain criteria unless justified by a legitimate aim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Crucially, this Bill does not protect workers against indirect discrimination, which refers to a policy or practice that while being neutral in appearance, results in a disadvantage for persons who may fit a certain criterion, unless it is justified by a legitimate aim and the "means to achieve that aim are necessary and appropriate".

sections.label: Disability Trends report inclusion findings
sections.summary: The 2024 Disability Trends report found only 53.5% of surveyed PwDs felt included and not discriminated against.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The findings of the 2024 Disability Trends report show that only 53.5% of the PwDs surveyed felt that they were included and not discriminated against.

sections.label: Reasonable accommodations advisory and UNCRPD
sections.summary: A non-binding Tripartite Advisory on reasonable accommodations would be released, but Government stopped short of legislating the right, relying on moral suasion despite Singapore ratifying UNCRPD in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, a Tripartite Advisory on Providing Reasonable Accommodations to Persons with Disabilities, which is not legally-binding, would also be released.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, the Government has stopped short of enshrining the right to request for reasonable accommodations into law, with Manpower Minister Tan See Leng articulating that it could result in heavy litigation and prevent employers from hiring employees that require such accommodations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This approach could be seen as being reliant on the moral suasion of employers and sends a signal that reasonable accommodations are "good to have" when it is a "must-have" for PwDs to carry out their tasks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, the new Bill must reflect that aspiration by legislating the right for employees to request for reasonable accommodation, especially when Singapore has in 2013 ratified the UNCRPD.

sections.label: Termination without cause in Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore employment law lets employers terminate a contract without cause by giving notice or paying base salary in lieu, with no reason required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Employment law in Singapore is such that an employer can terminate an employee's contract without cause, simply by giving notice or by paying the employee his or her base salary in lieu of the notice period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: No reason whatsoever needs to be given to the employee.

sections.label: FCF job advertising mandate
sections.summary: The FCF requires employers submitting EP and S Pass applications to first advertise the position on the MyCareersFuture portal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The FCF mandates that employers who are submitting EP and S Pass applications must first advertise that position on the MyCareersFuture portal.

sections.label: AI recruitment legislation and EU AI Act
sections.summary: A Minister noted TAFEP recourse for AI discrimination, and the speaker urges robust legislation, citing EU AI Act obligations on employers using AI in HR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a Parliamentary reply late last year, Minister Tan See Leng noted that candidates could approach TAFEP to seek recourse should AI usage result in discriminatory employment practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Instead of adopting a "soft touch" approach towards AI usage in recruitment, we ought to pivot towards enacting robust legislation that would provide workers with greater assurance and transparency with regards to how AI is being used when hiring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, the EU AI Act imposes obligations on employers seeking to deploy AI systems as part of their HR practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These obligations include, amongst others, instituting the right for candidates to request an explanation of AI's role in the decision-making process, ensuring sufficient human oversight over the AI system and adhering to data management practices that eliminate biases within the input data.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Bill and WP suggestions
sections.summary: The speaker says advisories and guidelines carry little weight versus legislation, welcomes the Workplace Fairness Bill, and hopes WP suggestions are considered before the second Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Advisories and guidelines hold little weight compared to legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am glad that we are finally putting forth this long overdue Workplace Fairness Bill, and I hope that the suggestions that my WP colleagues and I will be taken into consideration as we await the second Bill to be passed.

sections.label: Exemption for firms under 25 employees
sections.summary: The Bill initially exempts firms with fewer than 25 employees, and the speaker asks the Minister about factors determining the exemption period and plans to level up smaller firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While the Bill initially exempts firms with fewer than 25 employees, I would like to ask the Minister about the consideration factors that would determine the period of exemption and the Ministry's action plan to level up smaller firms.

sections.label: Voluntary opt-in and HR-as-a-service
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether exempted companies could voluntarily opt in for formal recognition, and repeats calls for MOM to introduce HR-as-a-service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Additionally, could there be provisions allowing exempted companies to voluntarily opt in to the Bill's framework and receive formal recognitions for doing so?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Smaller enterprises often lack the full range of HR capabilities due to resource limitations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, I reiterate my earlier calls for the MOM to introduce HR-as-a-service, similar to Infocomm Media Development Authority's Chief Technology Officer-as-a-service.

sections.label: Widening strategies for progressive HR practices
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister will consider widening strategies beyond award ceremonies, such as financial incentives, procurement quality credits, certification and spotlighting best practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Aside from traditional means to encourage progressive HR practices such as award ceremonies, will the Minister consider widening the range of strategies, such as financial incentives, Government procurement quality credits, certification, spotlighting best practices and scaling up existing ones?

sections.label: Managing expectations on workplace provisions
sections.summary: The passage states that managing expectations through accurate understanding of provisions fosters a harmonious and inclusive work environment and aligns with national values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Managing expectations through an accurate understanding of the provisions is essential to fostering a harmonious and inclusive work environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It draws a clear line on what is acceptable and what is not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is a positive move, one that aligns with our national values of fairness, respect and meritocracy.

sections.label: Bill enhancing trust and inclusivity
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill will enhance trust, support inclusivity and strengthen employer-employee relationships, and cites lower workplace discrimination rates in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If we do this, we can be confident that the Bill will enhance trust, support inclusivity and strengthen the harmonious relationship between employers and employees that is the backbone of Singapore's success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Workplace discrimination in Singapore has significantly decreased, with only 24% of job applicants reporting discrimination, compared to 43% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Moreover, just 8% of resident employees reported workplace discrimination, lower than the EU average of 11%.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Bill as milestone
sections.summary: The passage states the Workplace Fairness Bill complements tripartite guidelines, addresses discrimination across 11 protected characteristics and establishes a foundation for fair treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Workplace Fairness Bill is a critical milestone in this journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It complements the tripartite guidelines of on fair employment practices, addressing discrimination across 11 protected characteristics and establishing a strong foundation for fair treatment.

sections.label: Clarifying remaining complaint characteristics
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry to clarify what other characteristics constitute the remaining 5% of complaints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry clarify what other characteristics constitute the remaining 5% of complaints?

sections.label: Employees uncovered under 25-employee threshold
sections.summary: The passage asks how many employees will remain uncovered under the threshold applying the Bill to employers with more than 25 employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In Part 1, clause 4, para 2, WFL applies to employers with more than 25 employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: According to the 2019 Department of Statistics, 18% of companies in Singapore employ fewer than 25 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How many employees will remain uncovered under this threshold?

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Bill baseline
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness Bill complements the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices and sets a baseline addressing workplace discrimination across 11 Protected Characteristics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Workplace Fairness Bill is a significant step that complements the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (TGFEP) and sets a baseline to address workplace discrimination across 11 Protected Characteristics.

sections.label: Protected characteristics and disability legislation
sections.summary: The proposed Act defines 11 protected characteristics covering 95% of discrimination based on complaints, and is the first legislation specifically addressing workplace discrimination against persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposed Act defines 11 protected characteristics, taking a pragmatic approach to cover 95% of discrimination based on complaints to TAFEP and MOM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Before today, there has not been any legislation that specifically addresses discrimination against persons with disabilities in the workplace, making this an exciting milestone for many in the community.

sections.label: No indirect discrimination provision
sections.summary: The WFL does not provide for indirect discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The WFL does not provide for indirect discrimination.

sections.label: Employees seeking help for discrimination
sections.summary: According to MOM's Fair Employment Practices Report, in 2023 only 29.3% of employees who encountered discrimination at work sought help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to MOM's Fair Employment Practices Report, in 2023 only 29.3% of employees who encountered discrimination at work sought help.

sections.label: Reasonable accommodations denial not prohibited
sections.summary: The WFL does not prohibit the denial of reasonable accommodations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, the WFL does not prohibit the denial of reasonable accommodations.

sections.label: Job Redesign Grant support
sections.summary: Employers registered under the Open Door Programme can tap the Job Redesign Grant covering up to 90% of costs, with 50% reporting accommodations cost under $1,000 on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Employers will be happy to know that if they are registered under the Open Door Programme, they can tap on the Job Redesign Grant that covers up to 90% of costs incurred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fifty percent of employers who used the grant reported that workplace accommodations cost less than $1,000 on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Between 2020 and 2022, 20 employers hiring 60 persons with disabilities benefited from the Job Redesign Grant per year on average.

sections.label: Canadian Human Rights Act accommodation
sections.summary: The Canadian Human Rights Act requires employers and service providers to accommodate up to undue hardship, considering health, safety and cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For instance, the Canadian Human Rights Act provides that employers and service providers have a duty to accommodate up to the point of "undue hardship", considering health, safety and cost.

sections.label: Australia's Disability Discrimination Act adjustment
sections.summary: Australia's Disability Discrimination Act states an adjustment is reasonable unless it imposes unjustifiable hardship on the person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, Australia's Disability Discrimination Act states that an adjustment is reasonable unless making the adjustment would impose an "unjustifiable hardship" on the person.

sections.label: Decrease in workplace attitudes
sections.summary: A National Council for Social Service survey shows positive attitudes towards persons with disabilities in the workplace fell from 59.6% in 2019 to 50.6% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, based on the survey by the National Council for Social Service, there has also been a decrease in positive attitudes towards persons with disabilities in the workplace, from 59.6% in 2019 to 50.6% in 2023.

sections.label: WFL and Enabling Masterplan 2030
sections.summary: The WFL supports building a more inclusive society, and the law and its initiatives should realise the Enabling Masterplan 2030 vision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The WFL works in support of our broader ambitions – to build a more inclusive society, beyond just the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, the law and its associated initiatives should be harnessed to realise the vision of the Enabling Masterplan 2030, not only to meet the aspirational target of 40% employment rate for persons with disabilities by 2030, but to embed inclusion into every aspect of society.

sections.label: MOM Fair Employment Practices 2023
sections.summary: MOM's Fair Employment Practices 2023 report found workplace discrimination based on sex and family status was 2% for employees and below 5% for jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: According to MOM's Fair Employment Practices 2023 report, the incidence of workplace discrimination based on sex and family status across all reported discrimination was just 2% for employees and below 5% for jobseekers.

sections.label: Bill as safety net for workers
sections.summary: The Bill would serve as another safety net for workers outside the union network, covering protected traits and areas like sexual orientation and gender identity or expression through the TGFEP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Cases similar to Kelly's are unfortunately not unique nor one off and if this Bill is passed into law, it will serve as another safety net should our workers find themselves out of the union network and looking for redress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I appreciate the protected traits for sex, marital status, caregiving responsibilities and pregnancy and the coverage of other areas, such as sexual orientation and gender identity or expression through the TGFEP.

sections.label: Survey on reporting gender discrimination
sections.summary: In a survey of 3,000 respondents, 40% of women and 60% of men were willing to report gender discrimination they witnessed or experienced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In this survey of 3,000 respondents, only 40% of women surveyed, as compared to 60% of men, were willing to report gender discrimination that they had witnessed or personally experienced.

sections.label: Companies' anti-discrimination policy communication
sections.summary: Only a third of respondents say their companies have clearly communicated a policy against workplace gender discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Survey results also showed that only a third of respondents say that their companies have clearly communicated a policy against workplace gender discrimination.

sections.label: Clause on terminating pregnant employees
sections.summary: The clause stated the company reserves the right to terminate a female employee who conceives in her first six months and must disclose pregnancy at interview.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Essentially, the clause stated that the company reserves the rights to terminate a female employee should she conceive during her first six months of employment and she must tell the company during her job interview session if she is pregnant.

sections.label: NTUC support for SME workers
sections.summary: NTUC has 2,000 SMEs committed to fair workplaces, runs the Better Workplace Programme, and asks that legislation be extended to all companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To this end, the NTUC has been proactive in addressing this gap for our SME workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have 2,000 SMEs in our Labour Movement network now and they have committed to providing fair, progressive and safe workplaces for their workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Four years ago, we introduced the NTUC Better Workplace Programme, where we provide breastfeeding and wellness spaces to our partner companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In addition, I ask for consideration for the legislation to be extended to all companies in Singapore regardless of size in time to come.

sections.label: MOM survey on mental health discrimination
sections.summary: A MOM survey on Fair Employment Practices found mental health discrimination was the most common form in 2022 and among the top four in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to a survey by MOM on Fair Employment Practices, mental health discrimination was the most common form of discrimination faced by employees in 2022 and was one of the top four main forms of discrimination in 2023.

sections.label: Bill clause on protected mental health condition
sections.summary: Clause 16 of the Bill defines protected mental health condition as having been diagnosed with any mental disorder by a registered medical practitioner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: First, clause 16 of the Bill states that the protected mental health condition, in relation to an individual, means that the individual has been diagnosed with any mental disorder by a medical practitioner registered under the Medical Registration Act.

sections.label: Exemption for small businesses
sections.summary: MOM plans to exempt businesses with fewer than 25 workers from WFL requirements for five years after the legislation takes effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: MOM plans to exempt businesses who employ fewer than 25 workers from the requirements of the WFL for five years after the legislation comes into effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This is to ensure that smaller companies have sufficient time to transition and adjust to the requirements of the legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask how MOM would treat companies that deliberately set up multiple business entitles, all controlled by a single director and his associates, to get around such legislative requirements during the transition period.

sections.label: Covert discrimination against seniors
sections.summary: Although age is protected under clause 8 of the Bill, many seniors still face what the speaker terms covert discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Although age is explicitly protected under clause 8 of the Bill, many seniors still face what I term "covert discrimination".

sections.label: Mental health as protected characteristic
sections.summary: The speaker commends the inclusion of mental health conditions as a protected characteristic under clause 16.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, I commend the inclusion of mental health conditions as a protected characteristic under clause 16.

sections.label: Phasing out small-employer exemption
sections.summary: The speaker proposes phasing out the clause 4(1) exemption for companies with fewer than 25 employees as businesses grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The exemption for companies with fewer than 25 employees, as mentioned in clause 4(1), could inadvertently encourage some employers to keep their workforce artificially small to avoid compliance costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To mitigate this risk, I propose that we phase out the exemption as businesses grow.

sections.label: Call for workplace change
sections.summary: The speaker urges employees to speak up and seek support, and asks all to make the Bill a foundation for real change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To employees, speak up, seek support and encourage understanding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And to all of us, let us ensure that this Bill does not just remain a set of rules, but becomes a foundation for real change in our workplaces and in the lives of all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Framework for fair employment
sections.summary: Passing the Workplace Fairness Bill will provide a framework for discrimination issues and guidance for fair employment practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In passing the Workplace Fairness Bill, it will provide a good framework for issues involving potential discrimination and provide guidance for fair employment practices.

sections.label: ADHD disability coverage question
sections.summary: Asks the Minister whether ADHD is a protected characteristic if not diagnosed with the four disability or mental health categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister kindly clarify whether ADHD falls under one of the protected characteristics if an individual is not concurrently diagnosed with any of the four categories under disability or mental health condition?

sections.label: Broadening caregiver category
sections.summary: Asks the Minister whether the category of caregivers can be broadened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister clarify if there is scope for broadening this category of caregivers?

sections.label: Workplace harmony and fairness
sections.summary: States the workplace should not become litigious, as the Bill intends to preserve harmony and fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The workplace should not become a litigious environment as this Bill intends to preserve harmony and fairness.

sections.label: Reasonable accommodation under WFL
sections.summary: Proposes two aspects of reasonable accommodation to be legislated as part of WFL.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: As first steps, I would like to propose two aspects of reasonable accommodation to be legislated as part of WFL.

sections.label: Open Door Programme accommodations
sections.summary: Proposes legislating Open Door Programme grant accommodations as reasonable accommodations; the programme covers up to 90% of job redesign and training costs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Accommodations covered by grants under SG Enable's Open Door Programme should also be legislated as reasonable accommodations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Open Door Programme supports employers by covering up to 90% of the costs for job redesign and staff training to accommodate PwDs.

sections.label: Training managers and HR
sections.summary: Urges MOM to include training, supported by disability SSAs, in the WFL roll-out for managers and HR working with PwDs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Managers and HR departments working with PwDs must be trained to reasonably adjust performance appraisal criteria, particularly regarding what "working independently" means for someone with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge MOM to incorporate training programmes, supported by disability Social Service Agencies (SSAs), as part of the WFL roll-out.

sections.label: Accessible grievance handling for PwDs
sections.summary: Speaker emphasises that grievance handling processes, including online forms and physical spaces, must be accessible to persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: As WFL rolls out, particularly with clarifications on reasonable accommodations and what constitutes discrimination, may I emphasise the importance of making grievance handling processes accessible to PwDs?

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: This means ensuring that both online forms and physical spaces for filing grievances, whether within companies or with TAFEP, are accessible to individuals with visual, hearing or physical disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Without accessible grievance mechanisms, we risk leaving PwDs without recourse to address workplace fairness violations.

sections.label: Reasonable accommodations as fundamental enablers
sections.summary: Reasonable accommodations like wheelchair ramps are fundamental enablers of participation and inclusion, without which WFL risks being unfulfilled.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Reasonable accommodations, such as wheelchair ramps, are not just conveniences, they are fundamental enablers of participation and inclusion.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Without them, WFL risks being an unfulfilled promise, falling short of its true purpose for our PwD community.

sections.label: Protected characteristics cover most complaints
sections.summary: The current prescribed list of protected characteristics accounts for more than 95% of discrimination complaints received by TAFEP and MOM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For one, I noted that the current prescribed list of protected characteristics account for more than 95% of the discrimination complaints received by TAFEP and the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

sections.label: Administrative penalties for discriminatory employers
sections.summary: Employers found to discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics can be subject to administrative penalties at the first instance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Employers who are found to discriminate on the basis of one or more protected characteristics can be subject to administrative penalties at the first instance.

sections.label: Publishing enforcement decisions
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether the Ministry would systematically publish enforcement decisions, like the Personal Data Protection Commission does.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry be open to systematically publishing enforcement decisions, like what is done by the Personal Data Protection Commission?

sections.label: Reversing burden of proof
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether it is justifiable to reverse the burden of proof through a presumption linking adverse decisions to protected characteristics unless the employer establishes otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is this a justifiable case for us to reverse the burden of proof, through a presumption that the adverse decision is linked to the employee's protected characteristic, unless the employer can establish otherwise?

sections.label: Age discrimination prescribed age
sections.summary: Clause 21 of the Bill states it is not discrimination for an employer to prefer workers older than a prescribed age, apparently 55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, on the problem of age discrimination, clause 21 of the Bill provides that it will not be discrimination for an employer to prefer workers older than a prescribed age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Based on the final set of recommendations by the Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness, the prescribed age would appear to be 55 years old.

sections.label: Localising jobs Singapore Citizen preference
sections.summary: Clause 22 of the Bill states it is not discrimination for an employer to favour a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Second, on efforts to localise jobs, clause 22 of the Bill provides that it is not discrimination for an employer to favour a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident (PR).

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But what incentives are there for employers to do so and how do we measure the success of such each incentive in promoting a Singaporean Core?

sections.label: Penalties and compensation for discrimination
sections.summary: An employer breaching anti-discrimination provisions may pay an administrative penalty and be issued directions, with compensation already available for wrongful dismissal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Under the proposed Bill, an employer who breaches the anti-discrimination provisions may be liable to pay an administrative penalty to the Consolidated Fund and be issued directions to end, remedy or mitigate the contravention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Compensation for victimised employees is already available for successful wrongful dismissal cases raised with the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM).

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: There is no reason, in principle, why it should not be extended to other forms of discriminatory employment decisions whether at the pre-employment or employment stages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In fact, compensation may sometimes be the only effective relief if the relationship between the employer and the employee has broken down to such an extent that the employee cannot reasonably be expected to work for that employer again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am conscious that the detailed procedure for employees to make private claims will be addressed in a separate Bill to be tabled later in 2025.

sections.label: Discrimination watchlist and surveys
sections.summary: About 1,200 companies were on the FCF watchlist, an AWARE study showed widespread discrimination, and a 2020 MOM survey found race, age and nationality top grounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The situation at that time was not good, with some 1,200 companies put on the watchlist of the FCF for potentially discriminatory hiring practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A study by the Association of Women for Action and Research (AWARE) also showed that workplace discrimination is widespread, with about one in two Singaporeans facing such discrimination between 2017 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A survey by MOM in 2020 found that race, age and nationality were the top three grounds of discrimination.

sections.label: CPF equalisation levy on EP holders
sections.summary: The Government has been urged on many occasions to introduce a CPF equalisation levy of $1,200 per month on Employment Pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As a result, we have urged the Government on many occasions to introduce a Central Provident Fund (CPF) equalisation levy of $1,200 per month on Employment Pass (EP) holders.

sections.label: SME exemption enforcement assurance
sections.summary: PSP understands the need to support SMEs but hopes the Minister assures the exemption will be strictly enforced and not abused to increase cheaper foreign manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP understands the need to support small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in this transition, but we hope the Minister can assure us that this exemption will be strictly enforced and not abused as a conduit to increase the supply of cheaper foreign manpower.

sections.label: Bill excludes platform workers
sections.summary: Clause 3 of the Bill excludes platform workers from the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under clause 3 of the Bill, the law will exclude platform workers.

sections.label: PSP platform worker study call
sections.summary: PSP calls on the Government to study covering platform workers under the new law within two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP calls on the Government to study whether we can similarly cover platform workers under the new law within the next two years.

sections.label: Two-yearly review commitment sought
sections.summary: The Minister said the Bill will be constantly reviewed, but PSP hopes the Government commits today to reviewing it every two years after passing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister has said that this Bill will be constantly reviewed, but we hope that the Government will commit, today, to periodically reviewing the Bill, after it is passed, every two years to ensure that the protected characteristics are kept up-to-date and keep up with any new types of discrimination that may become prevalent.

sections.label: Race discrimination report statistics
sections.summary: MOM's 2023 report found race discrimination affected 1.7% of workers and 5.1% of job seekers in 2023, and a 2021 study found only 32.3% would report it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: According to MOM's Fair Employment Practices 2023 report, race discrimination was the second most common form of workplace discrimination, affecting 1.7% of workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Among job seekers, race discrimination ranked among the top three forms of bias since 2021, impacting 5.1% of individuals in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: A 2021 joint study by CNA and the Institute of Policy Studies on race relations found that only 32.3% of respondents who experienced racial discrimination at work would file a report.

sections.label: Support for race religion Bill
